facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells in an 'Indian file pattern', and positivity for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support this diagnosis.

The solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque and the immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for cytokeratin 20 and negativity for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings, are consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of cytokeratin8/18–positive and MNF116-positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node and the lack of evidence of primary or secondary tumors on imaging studies suggest this possibility.

rationales.F06: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement is characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma and extramammary Paget disease
rationales.F07: Tumor cells in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm are typical of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma and extramammary Paget disease
rationales.F08: Positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies supports the diagnosis of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma
rationales.F10: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration are characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma
rationales.F11: Isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node suggest metastasis, which could be from cutaneous apocrine carcinoma or metastatic breast carcinoma

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association with diffuse tumor cell infiltration, along with the tumor's histopathological features and immunohistochemical profile, strongly supports this diagnosis.
